lesson.title: Keep, archive, delete
lesson.subtitle: How long to keep it, backups that work, and deleting on purpose

video.title: Keep, archive, delete
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph — computer studies teacher, Kenya (main character)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Registers from 1998; Photos since 2010; Who decided?. Mr Joseph beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Our office cupboard holds registers from nineteen ninety-eight. The old computer still holds every pupil's photo since twenty ten. Nobody decided to keep them, and nobody decided to delete them.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: how long to keep school records, how to archive them, and how to delete them on purpose.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: The law and the ministry; The purpose: still needed?; A keep-until date.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A keep-until rule for every record
scenes.narration: Every kind of record needs a keep-until rule. Some rules come from the law or the ministry, like how long to keep exam results. The rest you decide by the purpose: why do we still need this?

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Final results: many years; Daily registers: a few years; Display photos: till it's down; Record, how long, why, who.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A pupil's final results may be needed for many years. Daily registers, perhaps a few. Photos for a sports-day display, until the display comes down. Write each rule in a table: the record, how long, why, and who deletes it.

scenes.visual: Icon cards: 3 copies; 2 kinds of storage; 1 away from school.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Records you keep must survive. Use the three-two-one rule: three copies, on two kinds of storage, and one away from the school. A fire or a stolen laptop shouldn't take the only copy.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Restore one file; Open it; It works.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: And test it. Once a term, restore one file from the backup, and open it. A backup you've never restored is a hope, not a backup.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Tables: CSV; Documents: PDF; Still open in 20 years; Columns, compressed: about 6 KB.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: For records you keep for years, choose open formats: CSV for tables, PDF for documents. They'll still open in twenty years. Store them by columns and compress them, and a whole school's term of attendance fits in about six kilobytes.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Which of these backups follows the three-two-one rule?

scenes.visual: Icon cards: The computer; A USB drive; One far away.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Two kinds of storage, one far away
scenes.narration: Three copies, on the computer and on a USB drive, with one kept away from the school. If the office floods, the copy across town survives.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Delete, and empty the bin; Wipe old devices; Shred paper; Log what, and when.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: When the keep-until date comes, delete on purpose. Empty the bin, wipe old phones and computers before giving them away, and shred paper. Then write in the log what was deleted, and when.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: SELECT id, kind, year … Caption: This term's deletion list
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A query can find what's due. Select the records whose year, plus the years to keep them, is before this year. That's your deletion list for the term.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: CSV, JSON, columns; Squeezed or not; Which to archive?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: same data, different sizes
scenes.narration: In the app, compare a school's term of attendance as CSV, JSON and columns, squeezed or not. Which would you archive, and which would you send over a slow connection?

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. We've copied the marks to a USB drive every week for a year, but never opened one. What do we really have?

scenes.visual: Summary card: A keep-until rule for each; Back up 3-2-1, and test it; Open formats for archives; Delete on time, and log it. Takeaway bar: Keep what you need, protect it, then let it go.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A hope, until you restore a file and open it. Remember: give every record a keep-until rule. Back up with three-two-one, in open formats. And delete on purpose, on time, and write it down.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Cards of school records; How long, and why?; Compare with the real rules. Dr Farah beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play “Keep or delete?”. Give groups cards of school records: registers, test papers, sports-day photos, report cards. For each, they decide how long it's needed and why. Then compare with your school's real rules.

options.text: Three copies, on the computer and a USB drive, one kept away from school
Three copies, all on the office computer
One copy on a USB drive

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — three copies, two kinds of storage, and one away from the school.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — 3-2-1 means three copies, on two kinds of storage, with one away from the school.

checkpoints.prompt: The marks are copied to a USB drive every week, but no copy has ever been opened. What do you really have?

options.text: A hope: restore a file and open it to be sure

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — until you've restored a file and opened it, you don't know the backup works.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a backup is proven only when you restore a file and open it. Until then it's a hope.
